title: Official talk
job: Announcements, offices and counters: the formal register you hear
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: THIS MODULE IS FOR UNDERSTANDING, NOT FOR COPYING. Everything on the left of it — the announcement, the notice, the clerk — is French spoken AT you, and the job is to recognise it fast. What you say back is on the right, and it is short and ordinary. Read the module in two columns and do not let the first one leak into your own mouth.

OFFICIALESE HAS ITS OWN IMPERATIVE, AND IT NAMES NOBODY. L4-M1's imperative is for people talking to people; a notice uses veuillez + infinitive, prière de + infinitive, merci de + infinitive and il est interdit de + infinitive. All four are followed by the plain infinitive and none of them has a subject at all — which is exactly what makes them sound official rather than bossy.

THE ANNOUNCEMENT TENSE IS ONE YOU ONLY HAVE TO RECOGNISE. le train partira, le guichet sera fermé, la mairie ouvrira — this is the futur simple, which this course has deliberately never taught, and it arrives here in the THIRD PERSON only, because that is where a learner meets it. Your own future stays L1-M6's aller + infinitive: je vais partir, never je partirai. Read the -ra ending; do not start making plans in it.

ENGLISH OFFICIALESE SHORTENS AND FRENCH LENGTHENS. English writes no smoking and mind the gap; French writes en raison de travaux, à destination de Paris, en provenance de Lyon — a preposition, a noun, and no verb anywhere. A learner scanning the line for a verb finds a noun and gives up. Find the NOUN first: travaux, destination, provenance, retard. That is where the meaning is.

THE SAME MEANING IN A HIGHER REGISTER IS A DIFFERENT WORD. attendre becomes patienter, and the queue's next person becomes au suivant. Neither is new grammar and neither is politer to say yourself — they are simply what the counter says, and knowing the pair is what stops you standing there parsing.

votre AND vos ARE THE POSSESSIVE THAT MATCHES THE vous THIS COURSE SPEAKS. votre for one thing, vos for several: votre dossier, vos documents. Every notice and every clerk uses them, and thirty modules of vous had never yet needed one.

pourriez-vous IS ONE FROZEN SURFACE, NOT AN INVITATION TO INVERT. docs/74 §2 keeps est-ce que as this course's question marker and that stands. pourriez-vous is learnt whole, like rendez-vous, because it is what you actually hear at a counter — and its hyphen is the only inversion this level admits.

sentences.display: Veuillez patienter, le guichet va ouvrir
sentences.cue: Please wait, the counter is about to open
sentences.literal: Be-pleased to-wait, the counter goes to-open

words.note: The notice's please. It takes a bare infinitive and names nobody, which is why it reads as official rather than as an order from a person.
The counter's word for L3-M5's attendre. Same meaning, higher register — you will hear it far more often than you will need to say it.
The window you queue at in a station, a post office or a town hall. Not a desk you sit at — that is L3-M2's bureau.

sentences.trap: veuillez looks like a form of vouloir you should be able to conjugate. Do not: at this level it is one fixed word that opens a notice, and nothing else in the family is being taught.
sentences.sound: vuh-YAY pah-syahn-TAY, luh gee-SHEH vah oo-VREER. veuillez is two syllables; the ill is a y sound, as in travailler.

variations.display: Veuillez patienter, le bureau va ouvrir
variations.cue: Please wait, the office is about to open

variations.display: Veuillez signer le dossier au guichet
variations.cue: Please sign the file at the counter

mistake.display: Veuillez vous patientez, le guichet va ouvrir
mistake.why: veuillez is already the polite form and takes a plain infinitive. Conjugating the second verb after it makes two commands in one breath.

sentences.usage: The line you hear before a counter opens, and the one printed on the sign beside it.

sentences.display: Merci de signer votre dossier au guichet
sentences.cue: Please sign your file at the counter
sentences.literal: Thank-you of to-sign your file at-the counter

words.note: A request dressed as a thank-you, and the commonest one on a French notice. Like veuillez it takes the infinitive and names nobody.
The possessive that goes with the vous this course speaks. votre for one thing, vos for several: votre dossier, vos documents.
The whole bundle an office holds on you, not one sheet. L3-M8's formulaire is the sheet you fill in; this is what it goes into.

sentences.trap: Merci de looks like gratitude for something already done. It is not: on a notice it is a request, and the thing has not happened yet.
sentences.sound: mair-SEE duh see-NYAY votr doh-SYAY oh gee-SHEH. votre loses its e before a consonant and comes out as one syllable, votr.

variations.display: Merci de patienter au guichet
variations.cue: Please wait at the counter
variations.changed: another infinitive, and the object drops

variations.display: Merci de signer votre dossier ici
variations.cue: Please sign your file here
variations.changed: the place becomes a plain here

mistake.display: Merci pour signer votre dossier au guichet
mistake.why: merci pour takes a noun — merci pour le café. In front of a verb it is always merci de, and the verb stays an infinitive.

sentences.usage: The notice taped to the glass, and what the clerk says while sliding the paper across.
sentences.mnemonic: merci de + verb, merci pour + noun.

sentences.display: Il est interdit de manger ici
sentences.literal: It is forbidden of to-eat here

words.note: Four words and one sign. The il is nobody at all — the same empty il as il faut — and the verb after de stays an infinitive.
The softer notice, one step below interdit. Same shape: prière de plus an infinitive, and no subject anywhere.

sentences.trap: English signs shorten to two words — no eating — so a learner looks for a French two-word equivalent and invents one. French spells the whole thing out, and the extra length is the register.
sentences.sound: eel eh-tan-tair-DEE duh mahn-ZHAY ee-SEE. est interdit links across the t, and the final t of interdit is silent.

variations.display: Prière de ne pas manger ici
variations.cue: Kindly do not eat here
variations.changed: the softer notice, and the negation wraps the infinitive

variations.display: Il est interdit de manger dans le bureau
variations.cue: Eating is not allowed in the office
variations.changed: the place is named instead of pointed at

mistake.why: the de is not optional. interdit needs it before the infinitive, exactly as avant does in L4-M6's avant de partir.

sentences.usage: Reading a sign on a door fast enough to stop before you have broken it.

sentences.display: Le train à destination de Paris partira du quai trois
sentences.cue: The train to Paris will leave from platform three
sentences.literal: The train at destination of Paris will-leave from-the platform three

words.note: Three words where English says one to. It follows the noun, not the verb: le train à destination de Paris.
The announcement future, third person only: sera, partira, ouvrira. Recognise the -ra. Your own future stays L1-M6's je vais partir.
The platform a train leaves from, numbered on the board. It is also the word for a quayside, which is where the sense comes from.

sentences.trap: The English ear waits for a verb and hears à destination de as a stall. It is not a verb and never becomes one — it is a preposition, and the verb is the -ra word much further along.
sentences.sound: luh tran ah des-tee-nah-SYON duh pah-REE par-tee-RAH dew keh trwah. The -ra of partira takes the stress, which is what makes it audible over a station tannoy.

variations.display: Le train à destination de Paris partira à dix heures
variations.cue: The train to Paris will leave at ten o'clock

variations.display: Le train à destination de Paris partira du quai deux
variations.cue: The train to Paris will leave from platform two

mistake.display: Le train à Paris va partir du quai trois
mistake.why: à Paris alone is where the train IS, not where it is going, and va partir is your own spoken future. An announcement says à destination de and partira.

sentences.usage: Catching the right train off a board or a tannoy, which is the only place this sentence lives.
sentences.mnemonic: Hear the -ra; do not say the -rai.

sentences.display: Le train en provenance de Paris a du retard
sentences.cue: The train from Paris is delayed
sentences.literal: The train in provenance of Paris has of-the delay

words.note: The mirror of à destination de, and the pair is how a board separates arrivals from departures. Again a noun where English uses from.
The delay itself, as a thing you HAVE: a du retard. L4-M2's en retard is the person who is late; this is the minutes lost.

sentences.trap: English says the train IS delayed. French says it HAS delay — avoir, not être — and a learner reaching for est en retard has just described a person instead of a service.
sentences.sound: luh tran ahn pro-vuh-NAHNS duh pah-REE ah dew ruh-TAR. The final d of retard is silent, and provenance carries its stress on the last syllable.

variations.display: Le bus en provenance de Paris a du retard
variations.cue: The bus from Paris is delayed

variations.display: Le train en provenance de Paris est arrivé
variations.cue: The train from Paris has arrived
variations.changed: the news is good, and the verb changes with it

mistake.display: Le train en provenance de Paris est retard
mistake.why: retard is a noun, so it needs a verb that can hold one: a du retard. est en retard would be said of a person, not of a train on a board.

sentences.usage: Working out from the board whether you have twenty minutes to spare or none.
sentences.mnemonic: A train HAS delay; a person IS late.

sentences.display: En raison de travaux, le bureau sera fermé
sentences.cue: Because of works, the office will be closed
sentences.literal: In reason of works, the office will-be closed

words.note: The notice's because. It takes a NOUN, never a clause — en raison de travaux — which is what makes official French so noun-heavy.
Building or repair work, always plural in this sense. It is the single commonest reason a French notice gives for anything being shut.

sentences.trap: L4-M2 taught parce que for because, and it takes a clause. en raison de cannot: put a subject and a verb behind it and the sentence collapses. Noun only.
sentences.sound: ahn reh-ZOHN duh tra-VOH, luh bew-ROH suh-RAH fair-MAY. travaux ends in an oh sound with no consonant heard at all.

variations.display: En raison de travaux, le guichet sera fermé
variations.cue: Because of works, the counter will be closed

variations.display: En raison du retard, le bureau sera fermé
variations.cue: Because of the delay, the office will be closed

mistake.display: En raison que le bureau a des travaux, il sera fermé
mistake.why: en raison de takes a noun and stops. A clause needs parce que, which is L4-M2's — the two are not interchangeable in either direction.

sentences.usage: Understanding, in three seconds, why the door in front of you will not open.
sentences.mnemonic: en raison DE a noun; parce QUE a clause.

sentences.display: La mairie ouvrira à dix heures
sentences.cue: The town hall will open at ten
sentences.literal: The town-hall will-open at ten hours

words.note: The town hall, and the office you go to for papers, a marriage or a birth certificate. Every French commune has one and it is where official errands start.

sentences.trap: ouvrira looks like a word you should be able to build from ouvrir for yourself. Leave it: this level reads the -ra and speaks je vais ouvrir.
sentences.sound: lah meh-REE oo-vree-RAH ah dee-ZUR. mairie is two syllables, meh-ree; dix heures links across the x, heard as a z.

variations.display: Le bureau ouvrira à dix heures
variations.cue: The office will open at ten

variations.display: La mairie ouvrira demain à dix heures
variations.cue: The town hall will open tomorrow at ten
variations.changed: the day is added in front of the time

mistake.display: La mairie va ouvrira à dix heures
mistake.why: va ouvrir and ouvrira are two whole futures, not two halves of one. Pick the announcement's ouvrira or your own va ouvrir, never both.

sentences.usage: Reading the opening hours off a door before you waste a morning on the wrong one.

sentences.display: Bonjour madame, je viens pour un rendez-vous
sentences.cue: Hello, I'm here for an appointment
sentences.literal: Good-day madam, I come for an appointment

words.note: Said straight after bonjour to anyone behind a counter. Leaving it off is what makes a French greeting sound curt, and it costs nothing to add.
L1-M10's venir in the present. je viens pour is the whole sentence a French speaker uses to explain why they are standing there.

sentences.trap: This is the other column. After six sentences of officialese the temptation is to answer in it — veuillez, en raison de — and it lands as a parody. What you say back is short and plain.
sentences.sound: bohn-ZHOOR mah-DAHM, zhuh vyan poor an rahn-day-VOO. viens is one syllable, vyan, with the n nasal and unsounded.

variations.display: Bonjour madame, je viens pour le dossier
variations.cue: Hello, I'm here about the file

variations.display: Bonjour madame, je viens pour un document
variations.cue: Hello, I'm here for a document
variations.changed: what you have come to collect

mistake.display: Bonjour madame, je suis ici pour un rendez-vous
mistake.why: je suis ici is understood but reads as a statement of your position. The idiom for turning up somewhere on purpose is je viens pour.

sentences.usage: The first eight words you say at any counter in France, and the ones that get you served.

sentences.display: Pourriez-vous patienter ici, s'il vous plaît ?
sentences.literal: Could-you to-wait here, if it you pleases?

words.note: Learnt whole, hyphen and all, like L3-M7's rendez-vous. It is the one inversion this level admits; est-ce que stays the question marker everywhere else.

sentences.trap: Seeing a verb and a pronoun swap places invites a learner to do it everywhere — venez-vous, mangez-vous. Do not generalise from this one surface: docs/74 §2 keeps est-ce que, and pourriez-vous is a fixed politeness formula rather than a pattern.
sentences.sound: poo-ryay-VOO pah-syahn-TAY ee-SEE, seel voo PLEH. The hyphen is heard as a link, not a gap: poo-ryay-voo runs as one word.

variations.display: Pourriez-vous ouvrir le guichet, s'il vous plaît ?
variations.cue: Could you open the counter, please?

variations.display: Pourriez-vous signer ici, s'il vous plaît ?
variations.cue: Could you sign here, please?

mistake.display: Pourriez-vous patientez ici, s'il vous plaît ?
mistake.why: the second verb stays an infinitive. patientez is a command, and stacking it on pourriez-vous asks and orders in the same breath.

sentences.usage: Asking a clerk, a stranger or a queue for one small thing, in the register they will answer in.
sentences.mnemonic: One frozen inversion, then the infinitive.

sentences.display: Au suivant ! Le guichet deux est ouvert
sentences.cue: Next, please! Counter two is open
sentences.literal: To-the following! The counter two is open

words.note: What the counter calls instead of la personne suivante. Two words, no verb, and it is addressed to the queue rather than to you.
Said of a door, a counter or an office. Its opposite, fermé, is L4-M2's — this is the row that completes the pair.

sentences.trap: Next! in English is aimed at a person. au suivant is aimed at the queue, which is why nobody looks up — and why you have to be counting.
sentences.sound: oh swee-VAHN ! luh gee-SHEH duh eh oo-VEHR. suivant is two syllables with a nasal ending; the t of ouvert is heard, unlike the one in interdit.

variations.display: Au suivant ! Le guichet trois est ouvert
variations.cue: Next, please! Counter three is open

variations.display: Au suivant ! Le bureau est ouvert
variations.cue: Next, please! The office is open

mistake.display: Au suivant ! Le guichet deux est ouvrir
mistake.why: ouvrir is the infinitive, the act of opening. The state a counter is in takes the participle-adjective ouvert, as fermé does.

sentences.usage: Knowing when it is your turn, in a room where nobody will say your name.
sentences.mnemonic: ouvert is a state; ouvrir is an act.
